title: Macalicious visual comparisons
description: Comparisons between rendered examples and crops of reference screenshots, and checks of states no screenshot shows. One file per component or demo folder, named <folder>.visual.json. The runner and lint apply these rules from visual/lib/spec.mjs, together with the ones a schema cannot say: budget caps, the tight companion of a loose comparison, the masked share of a crop, a comparison in each appearance, and, in the run, a 2x budget within the accepted slack of its score.

pending.description: Why the folder has no comparison with a screenshot in both appearances yet. Lint lists the folder as unfinished instead of failing. Remove it when the comparisons are in.

noReference.description: The appearance in which no reference screenshot shows the control, with the reason. The other appearance must be compared.

name.description: Unique within the file; used in output file names.

example.description: File name, without extension, of an example in this folder's examples/ directory.

windowState.description: Value of data-window-state on <html> for this run: the state of the window the example is in. Omitted or key leaves the attribute off.

selector.description: Element to capture. Default: #visual-root, the example's own box.

actions.description: Real input performed before the capture, in order.

hover.description: Selector to move the pointer over.

press.description: Selector to press and hold the mouse button on.

tab.description: Number of Tab key presses (keyboard focus).

key.description: Key to press, in Playwright notation.

forcedColors.description: Render with the browser's forced-colours mode on (forced-colors: active), as Windows High Contrast does. Only with expect: no screenshot shows forced colours.

crop.description: Region of the screenshot, in image pixels. Must be a multiple of the scale in both dimensions.

scale.description: Device pixels per point in the screenshot. Every Catalina reference is 2.

matte.description: Colour placed behind transparent reference pixels (window captures have transparent margins).

masks.description: Regions excluded from the score, in points relative to the captured element. For text set in the fallback font; say why in the description. Together they may cover at most 75% of the crop.

threshold.description: Colour distance (0..1) above which a pixel counts as mismatched. Use 0.05 for a comparison of the drawing alone (text masked): it shows a half-point change of a corner radius or of a hairline's alpha, which 0.1 hides.

budget.description: Highest accepted mismatch (0..1) per device scale; the run fails above it. Required for both scales. Set it just above the measured score: at 2x the run also fails, in Chromium on Linux where budgets are set, when it is more than 0.001 (a tenth of a percentage point), or three tenths of the score if that is more, above the score; another browser or platform reports that without failing. At most 0.25 at 1x and 0.1 at 2x, or up to 0.3 beside a comparison of the same example and crop that masks the text (everything this one masks, and more) and is within those limits.

deltaBudget.description: Highest accepted mean colour difference per channel (0..255) per device scale; the run fails above it. Required for both scales. Catches a surface that is slightly the wrong colour everywhere, which the mismatch fraction does not count. At most 16 at 1x and 8 at 2x, or up to 32 beside a tight companion, as for budget.

expect.description: For a state no reference screenshot shows: the size of the capture and the colours of chosen pixels, taken from the spec or the tokens. Used instead of reference.

size.description: Size of the captured element, in points.

x.description: Points from the left edge of the capture.

y.description: Points from the top edge of the capture.

tolerance.description: Accepted difference per colour channel, in 8-bit levels.

scale.description: Check this pixel at one device scale only (a hairline is half a point: only 2x shows it).

note.description: Where the expected colour comes from: the spec entry, the token, and whether it is measured or inferred.
